title: Key person insurance and buy-sell agreements
summary: For partnerships and multi-owner businesses, what happens if a partner dies, becomes disabled, or wants out?
detailsHtml:
Buy-sell agreements

A buy-sell agreement specifies what happens to ownership interests on triggering events (death, disability, voluntary exit, divorce, bankruptcy). Without one, a deceased partner's spouse may inherit the equity and become your business partner — typically a poor outcome for everyone. The agreement is typically funded by life insurance owned by the company on each owner, with proceeds used to buy out the deceased's interest.

Key person insurance

Separately, a business may carry life insurance on critical employees (founders, top revenue producers, irreplaceable technical talent) where the business is the beneficiary. Proceeds give the business time and capital to find a replacement without forced selling or distress.
